problem.name: Agnostic learning of decision trees
problem.statement_latex: Given quantum examples of a distribution over $(x,y)\in\{0,1\}^n\times\{0,1\}$ with uniform marginal on $x$, output a classical hypothesis with error at most $\operatorname{opt}_t+\varepsilon$, where $\operatorname{opt}_t$ is the best error of a size-$t$ decision tree.
problem.statement_text: Given quantum examples of a distribution over $(x,y)\in\{0,1\}^n\times\{0,1\}$ with uniform marginal on $x$, output a classical hypothesis with error at most $\operatorname{opt}_t+\varepsilon$, where $\operatorname{opt}_t$ is the best error of a size-$t$ decision tree.

strength.description_latex: Exponential or subexponential to polynomial in the strongest stated regime.
strength.description_text: Exponential or subexponential to polynomial in the strongest stated regime.

evidence.description_latex: The quantum bound improves a published classical algorithm in the stated regime; the comparison is between algorithmic upper bounds.
evidence.description_text: The quantum bound improves a published classical algorithm in the stated regime; the comparison is between algorithmic upper bounds.

hardware.description_latex: The algorithm requires coherent input access and fault-tolerant execution of the stated procedure; its circuit and workspace requirements depend on that access implementation.
hardware.description_text: The algorithm requires coherent input access and fault-tolerant execution of the stated procedure; its circuit and workspace requirements depend on that access implementation.

quantum.headline_latex: $\operatorname{poly}(n,t,1/\varepsilon)$ time by Chatterjee--SAPV--Bera, using a quantum Goldreich--Levin weak learner and agnostic boosting.
quantum.headline_text: $\operatorname{poly}(n,t,1/\varepsilon)$ time by Chatterjee–SAPV–Bera, using a quantum Goldreich–Levin weak learner and agnostic boosting.

classical.headline_latex: $\operatorname{poly}(n^{\log t},1/\varepsilon)$ time by classical agnostic decision-tree learning from examples, as in Blanc--Lange--Tan. Membership-query agnostic learners have polynomial running time with their stronger access.
classical.headline_text: $\operatorname{poly}(n^{\log t},1/\varepsilon)$ time by classical agnostic decision-tree learning from examples, as in Blanc–Lange–Tan. Membership-query agnostic learners have polynomial running time with their stronger access.
